question_text: A city in Metro Manila passes an ordinance that prohibits landlords from refusing to rent apartments to persons based on their sexual orientation or gender identity. A landlord challenges the ordinance, claiming it violates his property rights. Which of the following best supports the validity of the ordinance?

options.text: The ordinance is invalid because discrimination based on sexual orientation is not prohibited by the Constitution.
The ordinance is a valid exercise of police power to promote equality and protect marginalized sectors.
The ordinance is valid only if it has been approved by the Philippine Congress.
The ordinance is invalid because it infringes on the landlord's right to choose tenants.
